title: Isaiah’s stem, rod, and root point to Christ and latter-day servants
setting: Joseph Smith arrived at Far West, Missouri, in mid-March 1838 after leaving Kirtland. Between about 16 and 29 March, he answered questions about Isaiah 11 and Isaiah 52. An unnamed person asked the first three; Elias Higbee, a Caldwell County judge and high councilor, asked the others. George W. Robinson later copied both sets into Joseph’s Scriptory Book. They were first combined and published in 1853.
summary: The section is a set of questions and answers on Isaiah. It says the Stem of Jesse in Isaiah 11 is Christ. The rod is a servant in Christ’s hands, descended from Jesse and from Ephraim. The root of Jesse is a descendant of Jesse and Joseph who holds priesthood and keys for the gathering. Elias Higbee then asks about Isaiah 52’s command, “Put on thy strength, O Zion”. The answer says this means putting on priesthood authority, which Zion has a right to by lineage. Zion loosing the bands from her neck means scattered Israel returning to the Lord.

contextNote.title: Zion’s strength is priesthood authority
contextNote.text: Higbee asked what Isaiah meant by telling Zion to put on strength. Verse 8 answers that Isaiah spoke of people called in the last days. They would hold priesthood power “to bring again Zion” and redeem Israel. To put on strength is “to put on the authority of the priesthood”. Verse 10 adds that the scattered must return to the Lord to receive revelation. In this passage, strength is restored authority that Zion had lost and may regain.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 111–114 includes these answers about Isaiah. According to verses 7–8, what does it mean for Zion to “put on thy strength”?

newPeople.name: Elias Higbee
newPeople.why: Named in v. 7 as asking the questions on Isaiah 52; a Caldwell County judge and Far West high councilor.

jsp.title: Questions and Answers, between circa 16 and circa 29 March 1838–A [D&C 113:1–6]

reviewNote: Read all 10 verses. Official heading gives March 1838, at or near Far West. JSP treats vv. 1–6 (document A) and vv. 7–10 (document B, “Questions by Elias Higbee”) as separate texts; only A was loaded and is cited, and it describes B. The questioner of vv. 1–6 is unidentified. Exact date uncertain within about 16–29 March. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes. Setting checked against the official heading and JSP historical introduction.
